rhythm.cap.somewhat: Somewhat uniform — the rhythm barely varies.
rhythm.cap.fairly: Fairly varied — getting closer to human cadence.

home.annotated.hint: Highlighted spans are AI tells — hover for the suggestion.

ppl.gear.title: Configure server
ppl.hint: How predictable a language model finds your phrasing (its perplexity). Predictable, generic wording is common in AI writing — but formulaic human text scores predictable too, and stylized AI can score varied. A useful signal, not proof of AI.
ppl.url.label: Perplexity server URL
ppl.privacy: Unlike the rest of this tool, measuring perplexity sends your text to this server to run the model. It's optional and off until you connect a server. Nothing is stored there.
ppl.meter.title: Left = varied / surprising · right = predictable / generic
ppl.note.pred: Generic, easy-to-predict wording. Common in AI writing — though formulaic human text reads this way too.
ppl.note.varied: Surprising, less predictable wording — more typical of personal human writing (but stylized AI can score here).
ppl.note.typical: A mix of predictable and surprising wording.
ppl.error.unreachable: Couldn't reach the server. Check the URL and that it allows this site (CORS).
orig.pagetitle: Originality checker — find shared passages between documents
orig.tagline: Did they write it — or copy it? Drop in two or more documents (essays, a thesis and its sources, a batch of student submissions) and we surface the passages they share, highlighted as evidence. Edits like changed capitalization or accents don't hide a copy. You judge.
orig.privacy: Runs entirely in your browser. Your documents never leave your device — nothing is uploaded.
orig.text.ph: Paste or type the document text here…
orig.webcheck.title: Check the web for this document's distinctive passages
orig.web.hint: We can't index the whole web — so instead of guessing, here are this document's most distinctive passages. Search each one to see if it already appears online. Nothing is sent anywhere until you click a search. You judge.
orig.web.nohits: No web pages found for this passage.
orig.web.notenough: Not enough distinctive text here to spot-check.
orig.addfiles.title: Add many documents at once — a whole cohort
orig.needtwo: Add text to at least two documents.
orig.nooverlap.p: Across {0} documents, no shared passages of {1}+ consecutive words turned up. These read as independently written.
orig.band.high: High overlap — likely a shared source
orig.band.notable: Notable overlap — worth a closer look
orig.strongest.detail: {0} of {1}'s words appear verbatim in the other ({2} words across {3}). We show the shared text below — the call is yours.
orig.matrix.hint: Every document against every other — darker means more shared text. Click a cell to inspect that pair.
orig.pairs.hint: Ranked by overlap — the share of the more-copied document that appears in the other. Click a row to inspect the shared passages.
orig.pairs.none: No pair shares any passage of {0}+ words.
orig.pairs.hidden.one: {0} pair with no shared text is not shown.
orig.pairs.hidden.other: {0} pairs with no shared text are not shown.
orig.detail.coverage.title: Fraction of each document's words inside a shared passage
orig.detail.jaccard.title: Jaccard similarity of the two shingle sets
orig.detail.longest.title: Longest single shared run
orig.detail.nopassage: No shared passage of {0}+ words — these two look independent.
orig.para.hint: Catches reworded copies — same idea, different words — that the literal check can't see, and even across languages. This one is not on-device: it sends these two documents' sentences to the PeopleWorks server (EmbeddingGemma) to compare their meaning. Nothing is stored.
orig.para.needsentence: Need at least one full sentence (5+ words) in each document to compare meaning.
orig.para.none.beyond: (beyond the {0} already shown as literal copies above)
orig.para.found.one: {0} reworded sentence pair (semantically close but not a literal copy)
orig.para.found.other: {0} reworded sentence pairs (semantically close but not a literal copy)
orig.para.found.omitted.one: ; {0} literal match shown above is omitted here
orig.para.found.omitted.other: ; {0} literal matches shown above are omitted here
orig.disclaimer: This finds text the documents literally share — it is not a whole-internet plagiarism index, and shared phrasing can be legitimate (quotations, common definitions, a shared assignment prompt). Treat the highlights as evidence to review, never as a verdict.
drawer.web.title: What happens to your text
drawer.web.lead: These web searches are the one place a piece of your document can leave your device. Here is exactly when that happens and where the text goes — so you can pick the way that fits what you're checking.
drawer.web.manual.p: You click a Google, Bing or DuckDuckGo link for one passage.
drawer.web.manual.l1: What leaves: only the passage you clicked, and only when you click it.
drawer.web.manual.l2: Where it goes: straight from your browser to that search engine. It never touches the SignsOfAI server.
drawer.web.manual.l3: When it's over: close the tab and nothing lingers.
drawer.web.manual.fit: Best for unpublished work — a thesis, a manuscript, a draft you don't want sitting in anyone else's logs.
drawer.web.auto.p: One button searches every distinctive passage for you and lists the matches in one place.
drawer.web.auto.l1: What leaves: all of the distinctive passages (up to 8), the moment you press the button — no per-passage click.
drawer.web.auto.l2: Where it goes: your browser → the SignsOfAI server → the Brave Search API. Two hops off your machine instead of one.
drawer.web.auto.fit: Faster when you're checking many passages or presenting live. Because it sends passages out for you, prefer the manual path for someone else's unpublished writing unless they're fine with it.
drawer.web.auto.note: Automatic search isn't switched on for this server, so you'll only see the manual links below — and they find exactly the same thing.
drawer.web.bottom: Both find the same thing — pages that contain your passage word-for-word. The only difference is who does the clicking, and how much text leaves your device to get there.
